transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

The 4C code on Samsung washing machines typically means 'Water Supply Error' – the machine isn't getting enough water into the drum within the expected time. Since the drum is dry after a couple of minutes, this points to an issue with the water supply rather than a drainage or motor fault. Before calling an engineer, please try these two quick checks:
1. Ensure the tap behind the machine is turned fully on and the hose isn't kinked against the wall.
2. Check the inlet filter: Switch off and isolate the machine, unscrew the cold water hose from the back of the machine (have a towel ready), and look at the small mesh filter inside the inlet port. If it's blocked with grit or scale, clean it under a tap and reassemble. Let me know if you found any blockage.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Tap was open, I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway and no change. Hose isn't kinked. I'll try the filter now, back shortly.

Since the tap was on and the hose clear, a blocked inlet mesh filter is the most common cause of this error. Please let me know if you found any blockage in that small mesh screen at the back of the machine, and whether cleaning it fixed the problem.
Yes, the mesh filter was clogged with grey grit and bits of limescale. I cleaned it and refitted the hose, and now it fills normally and the 4C has gone.

That’s excellent news – it sounds like the 4C code was caused by that grit and limescale blocking the inlet filter. Since cleaning it restored normal filling and cleared the error, you should be good to go. To help prevent this from happening again, I’d suggest checking that filter every few months or if you notice the fill time getting longer. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

candidates: Blocked inlet mesh filter or kinked hose (high)
Tap not fully open or low water pressure (medium)
